newsitem.title: USA: Cosby asks California officials to rescind rewards.
newsitem.headline: Cosby asks California officials to rescind rewards.

text.p: Bill Cosby asked California officials on Thursday to retract rewards they offered to help catch his son's killer, saying he was grateful for the gesture but did not want taxpayer funds used for that.
Cosby and his wife Camille thanked the state of California and Los Angeles officials for offering the rewards totalling $87,500, but said: "We would like to request that they rescind these rewards."

"We do not wish to see taxpayer money utilized this way," they said in a statement issued by publicist David Brokaw. "At the same time, we wish to express our heartfelt thanks for their good intentions."

Last week the state of California offered a $50,000 reward for information leading to the arrest and conviction of the murderer of Ennis Cosby, the entertainer's son who was gunned down while changing a tire on a Los Angeles freeway.
The Los Angeles City Council approved a $25,000 reward and the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors posted $12,500.
The rewards have come under fire in recent days.
One Republican state lawmaker accused the state's Democratic Lt.-Gov. Gray Davis of offering the state reward as a "cheap political stunt."
"I really believe it's an insult to the Cosby family and crime victims across California," Assemblyman Gary Miller said.
Critics charge it was unfair to offer the money for the Cosby case when other, equally tragic, crimes go unnoticed.
A supermarket tabloid, the National Enquirer, offered a $100,000 reward for information leading to the arrest and conviction of the killer. The Globe offered $200,000.
